svg.text: How “a dog on a jet ski” becomes light on the POV column
No image model anywhere: Claude writes a short program, the program draws the frames, and the ESP32 paints them column by column.
Hold F9, say “POV, a dog on a jet ski”, let
go. Beeps mark press, release and done.
turns the clip into text; hot words fix
Claims the text file once, waits for 2 s of
keyboard quiet, then types the line into the
Main (a Claude Code turn) runs the pipeline
script. Planned: the router posts straight to
Scope: home, or public (“…for the video”)
with an IP-name check. A repeat comes
from the cache; otherwise a keyword
Sonnet 5.5 at low effort reads the scenekit
returns ~17 lines of Python. No image
Import allow-list check, then a fresh Python
process (20 s limit) runs build(): 90 frames
Loop seam, peak current at the worst of 96
angles (≤ 2.6 A), subject in the front
run-length frames, CRC32. This one: 37 KB
Simulator GIF and stills of the spinning
written to flash, CRC-checked. Then POST
File into RAM, every frame decoded, the
worst rotor angle found; the 5-bit LED
current is set so the column stays ≤ 2.6 A.
A magnet pulse each turn re-anchors the
clock: 96 columns per turn, 2.78 ms each at
A lookup table turns the flat picture into 2
× 168 LED colours; DMA sends 704 B per
8 strips share each row height, so every
point is repainted 30 times a second; the
eye (or a 1/30 s shutter) adds it up.
code built + host-tested, not yet run on the column

Measured 11 Nov 2026 on the desktop PC for this request (dry run, no upload): request → playable file 4.4–4.8 s with --fast, 2.4 s with --fastest, 3.7 s / 1.8 s from the warm daemon, 0.23 s for a repeat. est. = estimate from the code and datasheets.
